topic: Same thyroid dose becomes too strong after cofactors are fixed
angle: Fixing ferritin/D/B12 can change how much medication you need; retest and involve your doctor
hook: Twenty years on thyroid medicine. Then, in eight weeks, the same dose became too strong for her.
draft:
She took her thyroid tablet every morning for twenty years. Early 30s. A cold almost every week. Heels that hurt.

Her blood tests explained a lot: iron, vitamin D and B12 were all very low. Your body needs those to use thyroid medicine properly.

My job was to rebuild what was missing without touching her medicine. That part stays with her doctor.

Vitamin D and B12. Iron from day 10. Short home workouts from week 4.

Eight weeks later her iron had more than tripled and her vitamin D was about five times higher. The puffiness in her face had gone down.

Then came the surprise. Her thyroid test showed the same tablet was now too strong. Her body was finally using it. We had an urgent conversation, she saw her doctor, and the dose was lowered.

The lesson: if you're on thyroid medicine and still don't feel right, ask your doctor to check iron, vitamin D and B12. If you fix them, retest your thyroid. Never change the dose on your own.
final:
Twenty years on thyroid medicine. Then, in eight weeks, the same dose became too strong for her.

She was in her early 30s, catching a cold almost every week, and her heels hurt.

Her blood tests explained a lot. Her iron, vitamin D and B12 were all very low, and your body needs those to make proper use of thyroid medicine.

My job was to rebuild what was missing without touching her medicine. That stays with her doctor.

She took vitamin D and B12, and started iron on day 10. A few weeks in, she added short home workouts three times a week.

By the retest, her iron had more than tripled and her vitamin D was about five times higher. The puffiness in her face had gone down.

The surprise came from her thyroid test. The same tablet was now too strong for her, because her body was finally using it properly. We had an urgent conversation, she saw her doctor, and her dose was lowered.

If you're on thyroid medicine and still don't feel right, ask your doctor to check iron, vitamin D and B12 too. If you fix them, get your thyroid retested, because the dose that suited you before may not suit you now. And please never change it on your own.

#ThyroidHealth #WomensHealth

draft_v1:
One of my clients came in with a TSH of 6.09. Eight weeks later it was 0.35, on the same dose of thyroxine. On paper that looks like a win. For her it meant the dose needed checking, fast.

She's in her early 30s and has been on thyroid medication for twenty years. Her first reports showed ferritin at 8.1, vitamin D at 8.3 and B12 at 209. Your body needs iron, vitamin D and B12, among other things, to turn T4 (the hormone in the tablet) into T3, the form your cells use.

We left her medication alone and worked on those first. She started iron on day 10, along with vitamin D, B12 and magnesium at night. When her antibody test confirmed Hashimoto's, we added selenium and ashwagandha. From week 4 she did short workouts at home.

At the retest, ferritin was 27.65, vitamin D 40.7 and B12 367. Her TSH had dropped far enough that the old dose now looked too strong for her. Once conversion improves, a dose set for a depleted body can overshoot. We had an urgent conversation about it, and her doctor adjusted the dose.

If you're on thyroid medication, two things are worth knowing:

1. If your symptoms don't match your dose, ask about ferritin, vitamin D and B12 as well as TSH.
2. If those get corrected, retest. The old dose may not fit anymore.

Please don't change the dose yourself. Take the numbers to your doctor.

#ThyroidHealth #Hashimotos
